Messages.Author: The Doctor
Messages.Body:
I've been wondering about this one for quite a while.
It is both action modifier and combat cards. And the action modifier
part makes enough sense to be quite clear.

But the part where you get to use it as a combat card is where it gets a
bit strange. When you burn a vampire in combat, it is always empty,
since it burned blood to prevent it's destruction. So in that respect,
the combat bit would be completely and utterly useless (unless you
amaranth with just a few aggro).

I'm guessing it is supposed to be the amount of blood it had before the
damage was dealt, but I could not find anything current explaining this
card. Someone asked before, but this part of the question was left
unanswered it seems.

So, when you hit a vamp with 2 blood on it for 4 aggravated damage, and
play ritual of the biter rose, do your vamps get 2 blood or 0 blood?

//Doc.

--

>

and
> play ritual of the biter rose, do your vamps get 2 blood or 0 blood?

You get none.

You can actually burn vampire easy enough in combat with blood on them
left. Disarm, Decapitate is one example, 1 aggravated and Amaranth will
burn a vampire with blood on it. That new obtenebration card burn a
vampire with blood on it etc etc.

Note that when diablerizing the vampire eating playing RoTB gets double
the blood (once for diablerizing and once for the RotB). Also note
they're stackable, so you can play multiple on a single burn (only in
combat, since you can't play multiple of the same action modifier).

Messages.Author: Peter D Bakija
Messages.Body:
The Doctor wrote:

> I'm guessing it is supposed to be the amount of blood it had before the
> damage was dealt, but I could not find anything current explaining this
> card. Someone asked before, but this part of the question was left
> unanswered it seems.

Seems more likely that card is meant to do what it says--give you blood left
on a vampire you destroy by diablere. In combat, it is somewhat difficult to
burn a vampire by diablere when they have blood, but as long as you use
agrro and Amaranth (i.e. hit them for 1 agg, and then Amaranth them) or
Disarm them then Amaranth them, they are likely going to have blood left.

Even in the orignal Jyhad set, there are many ways to send folks to torpor
in combat when they have lots of blood:

-Wolf Claws for 1 damage. Amaranth.
-Ivory Bow them for 1 damage. Amaranth.
-Rowan Ring them. Amaranth.
-Pulled Fangs. Amaranth.
-Flame Thrower. Amaranth.

So yeah, to use Ritual in combat, you probably need to play Amaranth too.
But given that it isn't that hard, it makes Ritual somewhat useful.

Just to expand a little. the advantage of using RotBR in combat is
that they stack. I played this at the last Burton-on-Trent (UK)
tournament where unfortunately only 6 players showed. It was untested
but swept two games and got boned in th finals because the combat
chain (to give it a Cheryholmeism) is too long.

Crypt [12]

3 Constanza Vinti
3 Donal O'Connor
2 Theo Bell

Masters [16]

1 Giant's Blood
6 Blood Doll

Minion [74]

....and how often do I play combat decks. It was amazing fun though.
In round 1 my vampires gained 12 (2rituals x 3blood x 2vampires) pool
at one point, round 2 they gained 32 (2x8x2). Which seems wholely
reasonable to me.
